analysis.requirement: R5 — Feasible candidate facilities: Scenario C selects street-network nodes, not usable buildings, so the siting findings cannot function as implementable policy. Build a verified candidate-facility dataset (building/parcel, legal floor area, occupancy limit, filtration, accessibility/restrooms, staffing, ownership/availability, opening delay, transport access, capital/operating costs, pet/belongings/service-population restrictions); do not treat proportional capacity increases as physically feasible; report a cost-access-equity frontier, not only the mathematically optimal geography.
exists_defensible: Full, repeated disclosure that C's 10 sites are not real venues: manuscript defines them as 'algorithmically chosen street-network nodes' (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:184,188; docs/chapter/Capacity_Is_Not_Access.tex:589); results doc limitation 1 states 'street-network nodes, not real venues... no siting, zoning, construction cost or staffing is modelled' (docs/final/PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md:265-267); SUBMIT.md reviewer-prep answers 'Are the ten new sites real? No.' (per evidence inventory, docs/chapter/SUBMIT.md:302).

The data files themselves refuse to overstate: every new-site row carries coord_source='greedy_capacity_aware_p_median_over_rlis_graph', coord_confidence='theoretical_site_not_a_real_facility', provider='PROPOSED_NOT_A_REAL_FACILITY' (Geography/data/shelters/shelters_2026_expanded_plus_new_sites.csv:38-47, read directly).

A genuine partial candidate-facility dataset for EXISTING facilities: shelters_multnomah_2026.csv (48 rows, read rows 1-15) carries real street address, city, facility_type (congregate/motel/village/family), capacity with explicit capacity_unit, population_served (service-population restrictions, e.g. 'men', 'women non-binary couples and pets'), provider/operator, status and closure_date (availability), priority_vulnerable, and pets_allowed flags. This covers R5's ownership, availability, pet-restriction, and service-population fields for the real inventory.

Defensible occupancy-limit treatment for existing facilities: the unit-conversion table with per-unit ranges and named weakest link (family units 2.5-4.0) in docs/final/SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md:56-98, yielding the bracketed 1,885-2,224-person county total rather than a false point value.

The random-pool control materially reduces R5's stakes for the headline: ten random sites from the same 498-node pool reproduce C's sheltered count in every seed, so headcount credit is dispersion, not the specific optimal nodes (docs/chapter/capacity-is-not-access-source.md:238; docs/final/PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md:255-257, read directly) — any feasible dispersed candidate set would likely preserve the headcount finding.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "C is a buildable proposal, not a thought experiment."
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Directly contradicted 18 lines later in the same docstring ('New sites are street-network nodes: theoretical locations, NOT verified venues') and by every deliverable limitation. Nothing about buildings, zoning, staffing, or cost is verified for any new site; 'buildable' has no evidentiary basis anywhere in the repo.

The project's own results doc retracts this wording as an overstatement (PRESENT_DAY_THREE_ARM_RESULTS.md:15-20): no source establishes filtration at any facility and indoor air is unmodelled. This is R5's filtration field failing in the manuscript's own headline framing — the retraction never propagated to either manuscript form.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "the same 6,842 spaces more than halve refusals depending only on placement"
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: Implies capacity is freely relocatable. C's relocated capacity materializes as ten invented 349-space facilities, each larger than any real facility in the county (md:299), with no building, staff, cost, or activation path. The sentence carries no in-sentence feasibility conditioning.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: "The present 36-facility system shelters 30.1% of residents" (present tense, about the real system)
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The 2,234-space denominator is author-converted from five incompatible units using midpoints of ranges (SHELTER_CAPACITY_AUDIT.md:62-71), ~207 real spaces and 11 day centers are missing, and the figure is a model output under universal awareness. Hedged elsewhere (md:289) but not where stated — a reviewer enforcing R5 will read it as an unverified claim about real facilities.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: Deck: scenario C "the remainder opens as ten new ~349-space sites"
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: 'Opens' asserts deployability in a one-line scenario table with no feasibility caveat on the slide; the sites have no buildings and capacities exceeding any real facility.

claims_exceeding_evidence.claim: The md manuscript omits B's physical unrealisability entirely
claims_exceeding_evidence.why: The md's limitation calls B's 3.06x scale-up only a 'policy choice'; the statement that it is 'physically unrealizable for much of the inventory... a diagnostic bound, not a plan' exists only in the tex. Whichever form circulates without that sentence lets 91.6% read as an achievable target.

Minor count inconsistency: the audit that is the source of the exclusion records 11 day centers listed, the manuscript says ten. Trivial but exactly the kind of inventory sloppiness an R5-enforcing reviewer probes.

proposed_methods: Candidate-set construction by spatial overlay: building footprints joined to taxlots, filtered to public/institutional ownership and shelter-compatible zoning, floor area converted to occupancy via a stated planning standard (e.g. fire-code occupant-load factors), then attribute-screened for restrooms/ADA from facility inventories — producing a verified candidate table replacing the 498 geometric nodes.

Reformulate siting as capacitated facility location with fixed charges (MILP: maximal-covering or p-median with per-site capacity caps = fire-code occupancy and per-site opening costs), solved exactly at this problem size instead of the current greedy heuristic (scripts/build_scenario_c_2026.py), removing both the no-optimality-guarantee caveat (md:188) and the infeasible-capacity defect at once.

Multi-objective frontier: epsilon-constraint (or weighted-sum) over cost (capital+operating), access (sheltered fraction), and equity (mobility percentage-point gap), evaluating frontier candidates through the existing ABM; report the Pareto set, not the single optimum. The archived BS-sweep + B/C/CR/D runs already prototype the access-equity plane; the cost axis enters once unit costs are acquired.

Feasibility-capped sensitivity re-runs with the existing harness: per-facility-type expansion ceilings and a 175-bed cap on new sites, re-proving (or bounding) the 25.2% B-to-C walk reduction and the knife-edge result (C ~ B + 342 spaces) under realistic capacities.

Deployment-delay modeling: per-site activation lags sampled from the two observed 2020 lags (shelters_2020-09.csv) and operator-interview distributions, interacted with the tex's first-hour-race finding (80% of the mobility gap forms in hour one) — opening delay plausibly dominates siting for early outcomes.

Spatial block cross-validation of siting: split the 3,400 campsite reports by inc_date (column verified present) or spatial blocks, fit the optimizer on one fold and evaluate on the other, converting the disclosed in-sample-optimism limitation (md:297) into a measured quantity.

Cost-effectiveness reporting: cost per additional person sheltered and per unit exposure averted, by intervention type (new site vs expansion vs triage reserve vs awareness/outreach), so scenario D's zero-capital reserve result and C's siting result become commensurable for policy.
analysis.priority_rationale: R5 is decisive for the policy translation layer but not for the scientific core, and the repo's own control experiments make it unusually tractable. The comparative-diagnostic claims (capacity binds in A; dispersion rather than optimal geometry drives C's headcount; the equity gap is admission-rule- and scale-sensitive) are already framed as identity/direction results and survive without any feasible-facility dataset. What does NOT survive is every prescriptive reading: the present-tense abstract sentences, 'more than halve refusals depending only on placement' (md:319), the deck's 'opens ten new ~349-space sites', and the retained 'clean-air-capable' label — all rest on facilities with no building, no floor area, no filtration, no staff, no cost, no activation path, and capacities larger than anything real in the county. Two verified findings lower the repair cost: (1) the random-pool control shows ANY ten dispersed sites from the pool reproduce C's headcount exactly (md:238), so a feasibility-screened candidate set would very likely preserve the headline access result and change only the walking-distance credit — R5 threatens the magnitude of the siting bonus, not the capacity-vs-geography thesis; (2) the knife-edge sweep (C's siting worth at most ~342 spaces; gap gone at 1.1x) means modest feasible capacity additions substitute for optimal geography, which is itself a feasibility-friendly policy message the paper could foreground. Priority ordering: first purge the three overreaching wordings (buildable, clean-air-capable, present-tense system claims) — zero-cost, blocks the likeliest rejection quotes; second, ship the existing-facility candidate table and feasibility-capped re-runs, which need only files already in the repo; third, acquire parcels/zoning/costs for a true frontier, which is a full follow-on study and should be scoped as such rather than promised.
